title.en: Find tagged frames in the capture

why.en: Open the .pcap in Wireshark and show only frames that carry an 802.1Q tag.
why.hinglish: .pcap Wireshark mein kholo aur sirf woh frames dikhao jinme 802.1Q tag hai.

expect.en: Frames on the trunk show an 802.1Q Virtual LAN layer with the ID (10 or 20) and priority. Frames on access ports have no such layer.
expect.hinglish: Trunk ke frames mein ID (10 ya 20) aur priority ke saath 802.1Q Virtual LAN layer dikhti hai. Access ports ke frames mein aisi layer nahi hoti.

why.en: Show only traffic tagged VLAN 20 to follow the guest network.
why.hinglish: Guest network follow karne ke liye sirf VLAN 20 tag wala traffic dikhao.

expect.en: Only the guest-side frames on the trunk, such as the ARP broadcast and the routed packet leaving the router.
expect.hinglish: Trunk par sirf guest-side frames, jaise ARP broadcast aur router se nikalta routed packet.

why.en: In the ACL scenario the router answers with ICMP type 3, code 13.
why.hinglish: ACL scenario mein router ICMP type 3, code 13 se jawab deta hai.

expect.en: One Destination Unreachable (Communication administratively prohibited) packet from 192.168.20.1.
expect.hinglish: 192.168.20.1 se ek Destination Unreachable (Communication administratively prohibited) packet.

title.en: See which VLAN your own adapters use
title.hinglish: Dekho tumhare adapters kaunsa VLAN use karte hain

why.en: Home PCs normally sit untagged on one network; this lists adapters and any VLAN setting (read-only).
why.hinglish: Home PCs aam taur par ek network par untagged hote hain; yeh adapters aur koi bhi VLAN setting list karta hai (read-only).

expect.en: Usually VlanID is blank or 0 (no tag) and Linux shows no vlan lines. Output varies by machine.
expect.hinglish: Aam taur par VlanID khali ya 0 hota hai (tag nahi) aur Linux mein koi vlan line nahi dikhti. Output machine ke hisaab se alag hota hai.
